content: When editing a page, there is a small Summary field located beneath the main edit box. It is considered good practice to fill in this field, as it helps others understand the changes made, especially when reviewing the page's history. For section editing, it is recommended to add to the summary field to provide clarity. Setting your user preferences to prompt you when leaving the edit summary blank is also advisable. The edit summary box can accommodate a single line of up to 200 characters. If you attempt to input more than this limit, only the first 200 characters will be displayed, and the rest will be disregarded. For instance, if you try to add 10 characters to a summary already containing 195 characters, only the first 5 new characters will be included, and the remaining 5 will be omitted. The Show preview button allows you to preview the edit summary, which is useful for verifying links. It is strongly recommended to always fill in the summary field, as this is an important guideline. Even a brief summary is better than none. Edit summaries are particularly crucial when deleting text, as failing to provide a reason may lead others to question your motives. If you mention one change but omit another, it can be misleading; in such cases, adding and misc. can cover additional changes. Accurate summaries help others decide whether to review a change and often attract contributors with expertise in the area. While minor changes may not require detailed summaries, even a note like fixed spelling is appreciated. For small additions to an article, copying the full text of the addition into the summary field is highly recommended, as it provides maximum information with minimal effort. Use ft as an abbreviation for full text to indicate this. If the addition exceeds 200 characters, write a concise summary of the changes instead. For example, if you add 400 characters, you can copy the text into the summary field, and the first 200 characters will serve as a crude summary. However, only one line of text can be copied into the edit summary box, so further lines must be pasted at the end of the line. This makes it cumbersome to include bulleted lists in the summary box. A workaround is to place the list on one line, separated by asterisks, copy it to the summary box, and then format it properly in the main edit box. In addition to summarizing the change itself, the summary field can include an explanation of the change. If the reason for an edit is unclear, it is more likely to be reverted, especially if text has been deleted. For longer explanations, use the Talk page and include see Talk in the edit summary. Once the page is saved, the summary cannot be edited, so avoid spelling errors. If important omissions or errors occur in the summary, you can make a dummy edit to correct them. The edit summary appears in several places, including the page history, user contributions, watchlist, diff pages, recent changes, Wikipedia IRC channels, related changes, and the list of new pages. Using the enhanced watchlist allows you to see all recent changes to watched pages, not just the last change to each page. Experienced users often use abbreviations in edit summaries to save time, such as rv for revert. These should be used cautiously, as they may confuse inexperienced users, but they are generally acceptable for small edits like formatting or grammar changes. Refer to the Edit summary legend for commonly used abbreviations. The Wikimedia search function cannot search edit summaries, and they are not indexed by external search engines. When uploading an image, you can provide an upload summary. This serves multiple purposes, such as being part of the automatically created edit summary in the upload log, appearing in the image history entry, and serving as the edit summary for the creation of the image page. The upload summary can include a brief description of the image, internal or external links, template calls, and category specifications. The upload summary has a capacity of 250 characters, but the last part may be truncated in the upload log. There is no preview function to check the code for links, template calls, or category tags, but you can edit the image page after uploading to correct errors or extend the text. When adding a new section to a discussion page using the + button, the section title becomes the edit summary. When editing an existing section, the section title is automatically inserted at the beginning of the edit summary, enclosed in /and / marks. Details of the edit should be added after this text. If you provide a long summary, you can delete the section title to stay within the 200-character limit. When viewing such an edit summary, the section name appears in grey with a small link next to it, allowing you to view the section. If the section no longer exists, the link will direct you to the page. When creating a new section before or after an existing section by clicking a section edit link, delete the text between /and / marks to avoid confusion. You can manually include links to multiple sections using the /-/ syntax, which is useful when editing several sections at once. When starting a new thread on a Talk page, the Post a comment feature can be used. Clicking the plus sign next to the Edit link opens a box labeled Subject/headline. Text entered in the subject field becomes both the edit summary and a new heading, while text entered in the main edit box is inserted below this heading. In certain circumstances, an automatic summary is generated when an edit is saved without one. This differs slightly from the summary added when editing a section, as the latter can be modified by the user before saving. Automatic summaries are not a substitute for a proper edit summary, except when creating a redirect, where the automatic summary is usually sufficient. However, they provide some context for edits made by inexperienced users and help in spotting vandalism. Text in edit summaries renders internal links, including piped links and interwiki links, even when enclosed within brackets. Therefore, copying wikitext into the edit summary box may be preferable to copying text from the preview, except when saving space. Other wikitext coding is not interpreted. URLs are rendered as clickable links, showing the URL in parentheses. This provides the same information as in the wikitext but in a different format, along with a possible sequential number.
